reviews.summary: Jason found the 2026 Evo SLS a heavier, slower version of the Evo D/LAB that still boosts impressively for a 3-strut Dacron kite; his best SLS jump came within a meter of the D/LAB's. Progressing riders can time jumps and float more easily on it, but its pulling loop that can pause makes it a poor first-loop kite.

structured_review.summary: A very easy, well-balanced 3-strut Dacron freeride kite that boosted surprisingly close to the Evo D/LAB; Jason's best SLS jump was within a meter of the D/LAB's. Being heavier, slower and deeper in the window than the D/LAB makes it easy for progressing riders to time jumps and float, but its loop pulls and can pause, so it is a poor first-loop kite.
pros: Impressive boosting for a 3-strut Dacron kite, close to the Evo D/LAB on top jumps
Slower response makes the sweet spot and hangtime easy to find for progressing riders
Stable and well balanced for general riding, with a great low end
Versatile across freeride disciplines; popular with schools
cons: Loops pull hard and can pause or stall slightly before climbing
Heavier and less direct on the bar than the D/LAB
Slower in the air, which makes some board-offs and technical moves harder
Not recommended for learning first kiteloops
structured_review.best_for: Beginner-to-intermediate freeriders and jumpers who want stable power, easy boosting and multi-discipline versatility.
structured_review.not_for: Riders focused on learning kiteloops or wanting fast, technical in-air steering.
structured_review.rec_blurb: An easygoing all-rounder that still boosts close to its Aluula sibling.
